spec.title: ZAP runtime: Rust execution architecture and acceptance boundary

status.comment: Owner authorized Rust MVP implementation and publication on 2026-09-13. Existing Python behavior is prototype evidence, not production completion. NEXT execution and local Qwen inference remain separately prohibited.

p.PORTABLE-RUNTIME: The production runtime is a package-owned Rust workspace that exposes a typed application service, CLI, authenticated machine command and read interface, and cursor-consistent event stream. Ordinary build, install, execution, migration, and adapter helpers require no production Python, GitHub account, tracker, external database service, VibeVM source checkout, or UI framework. The future Qwik canvas remains a separate client.

p.PRESERVE-AND-EXTEND: Existing zap/1 imports and exact immutable bytes remain readable under their legacy codec and hash domains. The Rust store uses an explicit new store, wire, codec, reducer, and query epoch rather than silently changing legacy meaning. Canonical events and one-transaction indexed state follow spec://org.vibevm.zap/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-RUST-STORAGE#root. Derived exports, snapshots, and caches bind exact identity and never replace missing history.

p.MODULE-BOUNDARIES: Pure typed domain reducers are separate from transactional admission, storage and bounded queries, scheduler and effects, AgentHost, SemanticProvider, project adapters, backend protocols, and thin entrypoints. Pure reducers call no network, clock, model, filesystem, worker, or external command. Canonical JSON is validated at ingress and event-byte boundaries; reducers receive typed payloads. Every supported mutation follows one CAS, authority, policy, and idempotency path.

p.RUNTIME-GENERIC-PROJECT: Runtime project identity, sources, package capabilities, workspace, toolchain, commands, and user-local context are discovered or explicitly bound for the current VibeVM project. Host-repository paths, NEXT identities, operating-system-specific paths, and repository-specific commands are fixtures or configuration. Offline and container use remain valid adapters, and installation alone does not select a campaign.

p.TRUSTED-CONTROL: Owner and coordinator authority are established by a configured trusted application host or credentialed control channel outside the editable campaign store. No actor, model, role, packet, source, or result label establishes authority. Trust material is never passed to workers, stored in packets or public events, or inferred from filesystem authorship. The supported boundary rejects untrusted worker and caller input without claiming isolation from a hostile operating-system administrator or a process that already holds Owner credentials.

p.CONTROL-BINDING: Control commands bind campaign and BaseId, charter revision, expected Revision, RelevantBasis, exact action payload, and CommandId. Policy, semantic stop assessments, sticky pauses, delivery and safe-state acknowledgments, one-use exceptions, approach epochs, and combined charter and economics decisions survive restart. Admission is separate from simulation. A pivot, retry, packet rerender, or new coordinator cannot erase problem identity, authority history, or a pause. No active charter means no dispatch.

p.RUNTIME-SERVICE-ENFORCEMENT: The official mutation service checks typed command support, exact authority, revision and RelevantBasis, graph and obligation invariants, readiness, evidence applicability, stage duties, adaptive and economics admission, holds, stop state, and live-effect reconciliation. Scheduler, CLI, backend, and host adapters use the same predicates. Prompt text and direct edits outside supported routes cannot become accepted state.

p.RUNTIME-COMPLETION-PREDICATE: One shared completion-blocker query governs runtime and direct close. It includes unmet active obligations, integration, applicable stage debt and deferrals, missing required evidence, pending selected economics and Owner decisions, active holds or pauses, incomplete admitted effects, unknown external outcomes, and unpromoted required knowledge. Empty frontier, transport completion, or accepted children alone is insufficient. Dormant forks, DreamBranches, rejected alternatives, and untrusted drafts do not block unrelated closure.

p.ADAPTIVE-DOMAIN: First-class intent and outcome revisions, StrategicPlan and Lowering lineage, obligations, typed relationships, knowledge states, semantic assessments, forks, DreamBranches, task-contract versions, stages and debt, deferrals, evidence applicability, acceptance, and promotion implement the adaptive-cycle contract. A review may retain or revise a route only inside the charter. Atomic application checks captured inputs, explicit dispositions, essential guarantees, current work, economics, and stop conditions. Historical acceptance remains distinct from current applicability and value.

p.FACTS-AND-PROOF: The project adapter captures VibeVM specification facts and source identities separately from observations and acceptance. Source changes invalidate the known dependent closure while missing semantic edges remain explicit uncertainty. Accepted project knowledge is promoted into a bound permanent repository source; personal runtime state is not its sole home. Verification plans bind actual targets, arguments, cases, subjects, toolchain, and environment, and proof is reused only while applicable. No full product panel follows automatically from a task, stage, worker, commit, or publication.

p.RUNTIME-LOWERING-PROTOCOL: Checked lowering, pure capability rendering, strategic forks, weak round trips, and Dreamer scope changes follow spec://org.vibevm.zap/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-LOWERING-AND-DREAMER#root. Packets, roles, progressive disclosure, native host messages, goals, retries, and selected verification follow spec://org.vibevm.zap/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-AGENT-PROTOCOL#root. These contracts share canonical authority rather than creating parallel editable plans.

p.ACTUAL-RUNNER: A persistent coordinator selects independent ready packets and persists an exact DispatchIntent through the AgentHost interface. The Owner-selected evidenced native subagent adapter is the default; a harness bridge performs the actual call and returns an ExternalJobHandle and receipt. AgentHost remains distinct from SemanticProvider. The runtime never silently falls back to an argv subprocess, external launcher, provider, model, or account, and it reports unavailable capability truthfully.

p.RECOVERY-AND-RESOURCES: Claims, logical operations, packets, and attempts have stable lineage. Active or unknown-effect work is reconciled before resubmission; provider wait is not architectural failure. Retry uses recorded classification and provider guidance without resetting across process, context, model, or account changes. Read and write subjects, interface ownership, resources, leases, integration ownership, review capacity, and a fenced controller epoch constrain concurrent dispatch. Heavy commands use separately declared capacity. Stop delivery, process exit, and actual safe state remain separate.

p.RUNTIME-COMPACTION-RESUME: Meaningful boundaries persist charter and outcome revisions, plan lineage, fork grounds, stage debt, sources, evidence, packets, attempts, claims, host receipts, unresolved effects, holds, safe boundaries, and the next admissible action. A bounded resume view survives compaction, crash, quota loss, process or account replacement. Recovery verifies actual workspace and host state; it does not treat a summary, missing heartbeat, or unrecorded reasoning as authority.

p.RUNTIME-NO-LOCAL-INFERENCE: Until a future explicit Owner command, development and acceptance invoke no installed local Qwen inference, including discovery or smoke probes. A simulated transcript may demonstrate wire mechanics only and is labeled simulated. A weak local execution mode remains a normative capability without a claim that current Qwen quality has been tested.

p.BACKEND-CONSISTENCY: Clients receive machine-readable capabilities, revision-bound bounded queries, explanations, snapshots, commands, and event tails keyed by StoreId, BaseId, Revision, and cursor. Snapshot plus tail loses no committed event; duplicates, foreign identities, gaps, partial tails, stale pages, and unknown versions produce explicit recovery responses. Read-only clients need no Owner credential. Nonlocal binding requires explicit configuration; secrets and sensitive transport outputs remain outside views.

p.RUNTIME-CAPABILITY-TRUTH: Capabilities derive from actual handler, schema, query, command, AgentHost, SemanticProvider, and project-adapter registries and their evidence. Desired profile and resolved support are separate. Unsupported actions are refused. A planned specification, prototype command, fixture, generated GOAL.md, dispatch intent without receipt, or simulated weak transcript is not an implemented capability.

p.RUNTIME-TOTAL-OBSERVABILITY: The backend exposes the complete inspectable denominator required by spec://org.vibevm.zap/zap/flows/zap/ZAP-DATA-AND-VIEWER#root, including sources, strategy, lowering, packets, omissions, roles, jobs, proof, adaptation, economics, holds, stops, completion blockers, recovery, and invalidation. Opening a view performs no model call or new semantic transition.

p.CHANGE-ADMISSION-ORCHESTRATION: A protected change-admission orchestration operation may advance only the registered ServiceInternal assessment-adjudication and selected-admission records for one exact already-proposed assessment. It authenticates a credential already configured with the selected registered action scope, re-prepares the supplied comparison against the named store and revision, derives hold, affected jobs, effect identity and admission fields from current registered state, and commits each internal step under stable operation-derived command identities. Existing Owner credentials retain their separate exact decision/control role and gain no action scope. The operation never exposes a general ServiceInternal command route and never applies the product effect. Automatic eligible work returns admission-ready without another Owner decision; Owner-decision-required work durably records its hold and returns the exact decision boundary until a current bound Owner decision exists. Retry reconciles each internal command identity before advancing, while stale basis, foreign state, changed comparison, refusal and uncertain in-flight work remain explicit.

p.COMPOSITE-SUCCESSOR-CANDIDATE: A bounded composite successor preparation accepts only ordered registered milestone-create or milestone-revise precursor drafts plus one successor plan intent. It projects those precursors through their existing effect contracts, derives the plan basis and fingerprint from the projected state, validates the prospective plan with the ordinary milestone validators, and returns a stable request digest plus a dormant-candidate reconciliation identity without mutating state. A separate protected record operation authenticates the configured data-proposal channel, byte-reprepares the same request, and records only that exact dormant plan candidate through one narrow ServiceInternal cell. The recorder never mutates milestone heads or active plan state, never exposes a general internal route, and refuses changed content under the same operation identity. Actual milestone creation or revision and plan adoption remain ordered privileged plan.lower products in one shared comparison and assessment. Reader authority cannot record a candidate; Owner authority remains separate. Lost recording outcomes reconcile by the returned command identity and digest, and exact retry returns the same candidate receipt.

p.ECONOMICS-AUTHORING-CONTEXT: A bounded read-only economics context query returns the authoritative active policy identity, revision and digest plus applicable baseline candidates. It reports absence, a unique candidate or explicit ambiguity and truncation. Missing baseline pointer semantics never become a guessed latest identifier, and query bounds refuse before an unbounded policy or baseline scan.

p.MIGRATION-AND-RELEASE: Migration captures the complete shared or user-local MUP plan, every task contract and legacy constraint, original bytes and hash domains, and an exact identity, obligation, evidence, and authority-classification map into a separate recoverable Rust store. It validates before switching the store pointer and never starts NEXT. Release evidence covers isolated campaigns, native parallel work, restart and unknown-effect reconciliation, stop and economics precedence, lowering and Dreamer, weak-bundle fixtures, bounded large-graph queries, generic-project installation, source-only payload, and absence of production Python. Applicable receipts are reused; the final scoped package gate does not require an unrelated VibeVM product panel.

p.RUNTIME-PROMOTION-BOUNDARY: Temporary campaign specifications and prototype material may be retired only after unique requirements, decisions, behavior mappings, provenance, and accepted evidence are promoted to permanent project sources. Corrected Rust behavior uses its explicit epoch and is not misreported as byte-identical legacy behavior. Package release version, store and wire epochs, artifact maturity, and campaign completion remain independent.
